newsitem.title: USA: U.S. business inventories rose slightly in January.
newsitem.headline: U.S. business inventories rose slightly in January.

text.p: Inventories held by businesses edged up slightly in January as more goods remained on the shelves of manufacturers and wholesalers, the government reported on Friday.
Total business inventories rose 0.1 percent in January to a seasonally adjusted $1.01 trillion after dropping 0.1 percent in December, the Commerce Department said.

Business sales rose by 1.2 percent to a seasonally adjusted 735.93 billion after falling by a revised 0.2 percent in December. Previously, the department said December sales had fallen by 0.1 percent.
In January, manufacturers' inventories were up 0.1 percent to $438.15 billion following a drop of 0.3 percent in December.
At the wholesale level, inventories rose 1.0 percent to $260.80 billion after rising 0.1 percent in December.
Despite the overall increase in January inventories, unsold stocks of goods at the retail level fell 0.5 percent to $312.16 billion after being unchanged in December.
The inventory-to-sales ratio -- a gauge of how long it would take to sell existing stocks at the current pace -- fell to 1.37 months' worth in January from 1.39 in December.
The January ratio was at its lowest level since the department began compiling comparable data in January 1982, a department official said.
